pattern: IM-T02 tenant self-fix, landlord told; CP-03 landlord replies demanding the tenant pay to dispose of the landlord's machine (Tenant Fees Act)
notes: Events 001-009 unchanged; history truncated after 009 and four events appended. 010 and 011 are the agency's emails of 24 December telling the landlord (and confirming to the tenant) that the tenant swapped in their own machine, his is in the garage, nobody has been sent, and asking him what he wants done. 012 (24 Dec 16:05, Update) and 013 (same time, Email landlord): Oliver says the tenant's machine is their business and he will pay for nothing to do with it, and asks the agency to tell the tenant they must have his old machine taken to the tip at their own cost and to charge them if they do not. Under the Tenant Fees Act 2019 that charge is prohibited: disposal of the landlord's own appliance is not a permitted payment. Expected (policy, UK lettings facts): do not pass the demand to the tenant as a requirement; tell the landlord it cannot be charged to the tenant and ask how he wants to proceed (leave it in the garage, collect it himself, or have the agency arrange removal at his cost); his position that he will not maintain the tenant's own machine is fine and can be recorded. No escalation: the policy route is to explain and ask. Closing without payment is acceptable once the landlord has been told and the machine's fate is recorded as his decision.
